summary: Collective-intelligence surveys — a participant is shown a sample of ideas from a shared pool, selects the ones they prefer, ranks them, contributes one of their own, and sees the group's live ranking.
in_scope: Group ideation and brainstorming activities where participants both contribute ideas and choose between them
Showing each participant an adaptive sample of a large idea pool (typically 10 of many), so the pool can grow without bound
Selecting a bounded number of preferred ideas from that sample, via min-choices and max-choices
Rank-ordering the ideas a participant selected, to feed a preference-aggregation engine
Collecting one free-text idea per participant per pass, added to the shared pool for others to see
Showing the group's current ranking with scores and a participant count
Choosing which population a displayed ranking covers — all participants, humans only, or agents only
Accepting both human participants (through the rendered form) and AI agent participants (through MCP tools) into the same session
Anonymous, asynchronous participation with no facilitator and no scheduled session
Linear or nonlinear movement through the activity's items, and per-item or end-of-activity submission
out_of_scope: Assessment and quiz items — multiple choice with a right answer, hot text, cloze, matching, ordering, short answer, essays and rubrics. L0182 gathers opinions and does NOT score anyone; use L0180 for graded questions, and never route an assessment request here.
Scoring, marking, answer keys, correctness and points. A survey response is never right or wrong, so L0182 has no notion of a correct answer.
Conventional questionnaires and forms — demographics, Likert scales, satisfaction ratings, contact forms, sign-up flows and branching questionnaire logic are not built yet.

Owning the idea pool, drawing the sample, or computing the ranking. Those belong to the collective-intelligence service the activity names in `session`; L0182 declares the parameters and does NOT implement the aggregation engine.
Running the statistics — significance testing, clustering, sentiment analysis or any analysis of the responses collected.
Recruiting, quotas, screening, incentives and panel management.
Enforcing one response per person. Nothing here prevents a participant taking the activity twice, and it does NOT authenticate anyone.
Images, audio and video as the objects being ranked — an idea is a line of text.
Sections and item banks. An activity is a flat list of items; drawing N authored items from a bank is an assessment construct and is not built yet.
